name: humid_overcool_1694_run_end_coast_restore
description: The run ends (cooling -> fan): the lowered 75 is held through the 45-minute coast, then 76 is restored
notes: Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md Sec 10): (a) effectiveness: an immediate restore at the run end writes 76 at 14:20/14:25; no restore leaves the house at 75.

(b) docs-production: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md 'Humid overcool (Issue #1694)' states this rule; production applies it through humid_overcool.decide_overcool and AutomationEngine._command_adjustments (the one setpoint path).
(c) occupant: the house keeps its normal setting after the muggy run; a regression would leave the AC set 1 F low all evening.

Issue #1507 review (real-HA tier): the house reads 77.6F while the scenario's AC cools (at least the setpoint + 1.5F, so the real-HA simulated thermostat really starts its compressor and reports cooling, as a real one does) and 73.0F once a run ends (at or below its stop point, so it really stops); a cooling -> fan -> cooling blip under 5 minutes keeps the house warm. Each reading's humidity is recomputed so its dew point is exactly the one this scenario was written with.

verdict.summary: Held through the coast, then restored

events.note: Muggy house: 77 F at 64 % RH, dew point 63.9 F (at or above the 60 F trigger).
Hot day: the cool band 68-76 F is armed (cool 76 F).
The AC reaches 75 F and stops; the Ecobee runs its blower (cooling -> fan).

assertions.reason: One restore write, 45 minutes after the run stopped (14:20 + 45 min).
Held through the coast: a write during it would cut the coast sample and restart nothing.
Restored when the coast window closes. (Checked a minute after the event: a real thermostat reports cooling and stops on its own sensing tick, up to about 30 s after the reading.)

The run is over once the thermostat has not reported cooling for 5 minutes. (Checked a minute after the event: a real thermostat reports cooling and stops on its own sensing tick, up to about 30 s after the reading.)
